memory_update.text: POWL should remain a high-priority underfollowed candidate for this node because it has direct medium-voltage switchgear and engineered power-distribution exposure, explicit data-center demand commentary, and a disclosed >$400M data-center order in FY2026.
BELFB is a lower-attention magnetics/power-conversion candidate; keep it in Layer 1 with evidence-needed flags around financial materiality of networking/cloud and industrial electrification demand.

PLPC is not a transformer maker but fits the speculative-shadow lane as utility T&D hardware that may benefit from the same grid-capex bottleneck; survival in later layers requires current 10-K validation of revenue exposure, qualification cycles, and backlog sensitivity.

For transformers_power_distribution_magnetics, adjacent chokepoints include medium-voltage switchgear, electrical houses, power-control rooms, discrete magnetics, power supplies, utility T&D line hardware, distribution automation, and substation connectors.

Potential non-US or OTC transformer pure plays such as Hammond Power Solutions may be highly relevant but were not included because this pass requested US-listed companies; later global-listed pass should revisit HPS.A/HMDPF and other Canada/India transformer and power-quality suppliers.

summary: Layer 1B expanded the universe around transformer-adjacent power distribution, magnetics, medium-voltage switchgear, utility T&D hardware, and power-quality components. The strongest underfollowed US-listed candidates in this pass are Powell Industries for medium-voltage/data-center electrical distribution, Bel Fuse for magnetics/power transformers/power supplies, and Preformed Line Products as a second-order transmission/distribution hardware chokepoint. Hubbell is included as a higher-attention reference anchor because it has explicit utility transmission, substation, and distribution exposure but is less underfollowed and less pure.
